newsitem.title: UK: LCE robusta futures off highs, well supported.
newsitem.headline: LCE robusta futures off highs, well supported.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures on Monday recovered some lost ground on industry buying after sinking last week to four-week lows of $1,520 a tonne, traders said.
"There has been some good industry support...But overall, prices are expected to drift," said one trader.
Robusta prices have been slapped down from a high of $1,740 on August 27 after a buildup in US speculative long positions and forecasts for higher supply in the 1996/97 season.
At midday the benchmark November contract was up $12 at $1,546 a tonne but off a session high of $1,554 a tonne.
Turnover on the exchange reached 1,365 lots.
While prices are seen well supported, on the upside the contract faces steep resistance at $1,580 a tonne and chartists forecast a slide if key resistance is not breached.
"My feeling is it's going to head down towards the key support of $1,450," said Richard Gardiner, technical analyst at Gerald Ltd.

Traders said prices should remain supported with New York's arabica contract firm on news of possible delays in Colombian coffee exports due to trucker protests, crumbling infrastructure and leftist guerrilla attacks.

"There is certainly no doubt that Colombian shipments have been delayed at least two days due to guerrilla activity. And while force majeure has not been declared yet, there are no signs military activity will die down in the short-term," broker GNI said on Monday.
